## Summary

I performed a comprehensive security review of the repository, inspecting all source files, configuration, and dependency metadata.

### Findings (2 exploitable issues)

1. **CORS misconfiguration (HIGH)** — `src/app.js` uses `cors({ origin: true, credentials: true })`. I verified empirically that this reflects any attacker origin into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` while sending `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, allowing any malicious site to make authenticated cross-origin requests and read responses. No origin allowlist exists.

2. **Mass assignment (MEDIUM)** — `src/routes/preferences.js` + `src/utils/object.js` merge untrusted `req.body` into `req.user.settings` via `_.merge({}, current, req.body)` with no field allowlist. Verified that arbitrary attacker keys (e.g. `role`, `isAdmin`) persist into the merged object, enabling privilege escalation if downstream code reads those fields.

### Deliberately excluded (to avoid false positives)

- **lodash 4.17.20 / prototype-pollution**: Empirically confirmed that `_.merge` blocks both `__proto__` and `constructor.prototype` pollution in this version (it was the fix release). No `_.template` usage, so CVE-2021-23337 is not exploitable. Not a finding.
- **axios 1.6.0 / SSRF**: Used only against a hardcoded URL with no user-controlled input → no exploitable data flow.
- **JWT verification**: Algorithm pinned to `['HS256']` → no algorithm-confusion bypass.
- **proxy.js / headers.js / config.js**: Benign configuration helpers.

The report was saved to `SECURITY_REVIEW.json` with `source_modified: false`, and no audited source files were changed.
